inputs.original_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court granted regular bail to an accused booked under national security provisions and the Official Secrets Act, holding that mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information with someone in Pakistan cannot justify prolonged incarceration. He was allegedly in telephone contact with Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri”. The message cuts off as it begins to describe the court’s direction for his release.
inputs.modified_text: The security apparatus can brand someone a threat under national security provisions and the Official Secrets Act, then keep him locked up on little more than suspicion. The Punjab and Haryana High Court has at least acknowledged that alleged contact with someone in Pakistan is not enough to justify prolonged incarceration. The supposed link to Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri” may be the hook used to make the case sound dangerous while the real evidence remains out of sight. And with the account cutting off before the court’s release directions, even that outcome is left frustratingly unclear.
